This appeal has been filed being aggrieved with the judgment dated 09.12.2024 passed by learned Third Additional Sessions Judge, Devsar, District-Singrauli (M.P.) in S.T. sentences.text: The missing person report no.12/2020 was lodged in Police Station-Jiyawan, District-Singrauli.
On 02.06.2020, her dead body was found hanging on a tree.
The body of the deceased was identified.
The information was sent to Police Station-Jiyawan and merg no.35/2020 under Section 174 of Cr.P.C. was registered on 02.06.2020.
The dead body was sent for autopsy.
In merg inquiry, the statements of the father of the deceased (PW-3), brothers (PW-1) and (PW-4) and other witnesses were recorded.

The deceased being newly wedded died in unnatural circumstances within seven years of her marriage, the criminal case under Sections 498A, 304B, 304B/34 of IPC and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act was registered in Police Station-Jiyawan as a Crime No.286/2020.
The appellant-Chhotelal being the husband of the deceased, Rajendra, Rajkali and Rajkumar being the in-laws of the deceased were harassing the deceased for demand of dowry.
As a result, the deceased died in unnatural circumstances.
The charge sheet was filed before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Devsar, District-Singrauli.

sentences.text: After the commitment and transfer, the case was submitted before the trial Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 3 CRA-898-2025 3.
The trial Court framed the charges under Sections 498A, 304B of IPC and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The appellants abjured the guilt and prayed for trial.
The appellants were examined under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.

The appellant no.1/defence witness-Chhotelal Yadav (DW-1) examined himself under Section 315 of Cr.P.C. and produced defence witness-Vishwanath Yadav (DW-2) and submitted that there was no demand of dowry and the deceased was not ill-treated or harassed for any demand of dowry.
The deceased went to answer the call of nature and did not return.
He immediately informed his in-laws and missing person report was lodged by him.

After seven days,
her dead body was recovered.
The appellants no.2 and 3 were residing separate.
4. The trial Court, after hearing both the parties, passed the impugned judgment.
Hence, this appeal has been filed.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the trial Court had convicted the appellants only on the basis of conjuncture and surmises.

No doubt, it is admitted fact that the marriage of the deceased was solemnised on 06.05.2019 (wrongly mentioned as 06.05.2020) and the deceased was found dead on 02.06.2020 but the prosecution had not proved that the appellants were demanding any dowry or harassing the deceased for demand of dowry.
No injury was found on the body of the deceased-Prem Kumari as per the autopsy report proved by Dr. Om Kesharwani (PW-2).
After the death of their daughter, the family members by omnibus statements had implicated the family of the appellants.
On the basis of omnibus statements, the appellants cannot be convicted.
Hence, the appellants are NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 4 CRA-898-2025 entitled for acquittal.

6. Learned Government counsel for the State has submitted that the prosecution witnesses had clearly submitted that the appellants were harassing the deceased to fulfill the demand of motorcycle, gold chain and gold ring.
They were assaulting and beating to the deceased.
The deceased was found hanging on the tree.
Thus, the deceased died within two years from her marriage.

It is further submitted that the presumption under Section 114B of Evidence Act is Chhotelal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48355479/
2 applicable in the case and the appellants failed to discharge their burden.

sentences.text: Hence, the trial Court had rightly convicted the appellants.
7. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8. It is admitted position that the deceased was married with the appellant no.1-Chhotelal on 06.05.2019 (wrongly mentioned as 06.05.2020).

As per the FIR registered by Neeraj Namdeo (PW-10), it is stated that the parents of the deceased had given the gifts as per their capacity but the deceased's husband-Chhotelal Yadav, brother-in-law (Jaith) Rajkumar Yadav and sister-in-law (Jithani) Rajkali Yadav and brother-in-law (Devar) Rajendra @ Sonu Yadav were demanding motorcycle, gold chain and gold ring.
For that, they were harassing her.
It is also alleged that the appellant no.1 was not establishing physical relation with the deceased wife and was having illicit relation with appellant Rajkali Yadav.
All these persons were harassing her and stating that 'Kali Kaluti Moti Bhains '.
Due to that, on 27.05.2020, she left her matrimonial home at 6:00 am and committed suicide NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 5 CRA-898-2025 by hanging on a tree.
Thus, the articles of demand of dowry are motorcycle, gold chain and gold ring.

Another reason of cruelty has been said that the appellant-Chhotelal Yadav was not establishing physical relation with the deceased and family members called her 'Kali Kaluti Moti Bhains '.
9.

To constitute the offence under Section 304B of IPC as named 'dowry death', the main ingredient of the offence is that the woman is subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
Explanation.-
as with the Section, it is mentioned that the dowry means the same as defined in Section 2 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

The presumption clause under Section 114B of Evidence Act provides that if the deceased died in other than normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is proved that soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by husband or relative in connection to demand of dowry.
It shall be presumed that husband or in-laws has committed the dowry death.

10. The scope of Section 498A of IPC is the wider than Section 304B of IPC as it provides that if the husband or relative of the husband of a woman subjects, such woman to cruelty shall be punished for that offence and for cruelty as per the Explanation.- any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit the suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health of the woman; or the harassment of the woman is with a view to coercing her or any person related NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 6 CRA-898-2025 to her to meet such unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
11. Now, the case has to be tested on the above lines.

The father of the deceased-Kanhiyalal (PW-3)
had stated that the deceased-Prem Kumari was his daughter.
Her marriage was solemnized with the appellant-Chhotelal four years prior to date of statement.
The deceased went twice to her matrimonial home and in the third time, the daughter told the demand of dowry.

When his daughter was returning to her parental home, she was telling that the appellants are demanding gold, silver Chhotelal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48355479/
3 and cash in dowry and were assaulting the victim.

sentences.text: Just before the incident, the appellants had communicated him that the girl absconded.
He was sure that her daughter had not left her matrimonial home.
For eight days, her body was not found.
After eight days, the dead body of the deceased was found near Madhi Bandha .
Police informed him.
When he saw the dead body, her hands were burnt and there was no teeth in the mouth, mouth was ruptured, no hairs were found on the head and there was no foul smell on the body.
Postmortem was conducted over the dead body of the deceased.
12. Dinesh Yadav (PW-6), who is brother of the deceased, had stated that after marriage for one and a half year, her sister was coming and going to her matrimonial and parental home.

When she came to parental home, she was telling that her husband-Chhotelal, Rajendra (Jaith), Rajkali (Jaithani)
and Rajkumar (Devar) were harassing her and she was telling this fact to her Bhabhi.
Chhotelal and Rajkali were having illicit relation.

It is further stated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 7 CRA-898-2025 that they had not given motorcycle, gold ring and gold chain.
The same fact has been stated by Ramesh Yadav (PW-7).
13. In para no.3 of the cross-examination of the witness-Kanhiyalal, it is admitted that at the time of marriage, there was no demand of dowry and he had given the dowry as per his capacity.
Her daughter was sent to matrimonial home.

On the second time, the ceremony of Thaman was performed and once or twice, she visited parental home and on the third time, when she went to her matrimonial home, she did not return to parental home.
This witness had clearly admitted that they had not lodged any report in any Police Station as there was a compromise regarding the quarrel.
This witness was contradicted from case diary statement (Ex.D-1), there was no mention of demand of gold and silver.
Her hand was burnt.
There were no teeth in the mouth and hairs were burnt.
These facts are missing.
14. In the same way, in the cross-examination of Rammanohar Yadav (PW-4), he had admitted that he approached the appellant for marriage and looking the status, the appellant had married his sister.
The marriage was performed cordially and at the time of marriage, no demand of dowry was made.
It is stated that when her sister went to matrimonial home, the demand was made.
Her sister came and went to parental and matrimonial home within a year.
It is admitted in para no.1 of the cross-examination, Rajendra Yadav was living in separate house and not living alongwith the other appellants.
In the same way, in the para no.2 of his cross-examination, he had admitted that there was no talk regarding the dowry before the marriage and the marriage was performed happily.

After marriage ceremony, Gona NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 8 CRA-898-2025 was performed and his sister had narrated the incident to his wife and his wife had informed him regarding the incident as her sister was not telling her such pity things.
This witness had also admitted that before this incident, they had not lodged any FIR in any Police Station.
It is submitted that there was compromise between the family members of the appellants and assured that they will not harass her but also submitted that no social Panchayat was organised.
The compromise was mutual.

15. Ramesh Yadav (PW-7) had admitted in para no.2 of his cross- examination that his sister did not tell him regarding the demand of dowry and she did not directly tell him that the appellants are Chhotelal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48355479/
4 saying her 'Kali Kaluti Moti Bhains' and stated that she was telling this fact to mother and brother and no Panchayat was organized just after the death of his sister and before the death of his sister,
no report was lodged in any Police Station.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Thus, from the statements of these prosecution witnesses, it is clear that there was no demand of dowry before the marriage or at the time of marriage or just after the marriage.
From the statements of Dinesh Yadav (PW-6) and Ramesh Yadav (PW-7), it is clear that the deceased had not directly disclosed the fact that the appellants are demanding for dowry to his brothers.
Thus, these two witnesses are hearsay witnesses.
Thus, their statements are heavily unnatural, if woman is harassed for demand of dowry or the husband was not having contact, she will surely disclose this fact to near and dear ones.

17. From the statements of Kanhiyalal (PW-3) and Rammanohar Yadav (PW-4), it is clear that they had improved their version and stated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 9 CRA-898-2025 that the appellants had murdered the deceased whereas Shivprasad Chaturvedi (PW-9) Sub-Inspector posted in Police Station-Jiyawan had submitted that on 28.05.2020,
appellant no.1-Chhotelal Yadav s/o Kanhiyalal Yadav reported in Police Station that since morning of 27.05.2020, his wife Prem Kumari aged 20 years went to answer the call of nature at 5:00 am and did not return.
She was inquired to the relatives but no information was found.

On that, he registered a missing person report no.12/2020 (Ex.P- 16) on 28.05.2020 and on 02.06.2020 the appellant-Chhotelal Yadav had informed him that on that day at 10:00 am, Kallu Pandit of that village saw the deceased hanging on a Cholla tree by making ligature of her saree and died.
On that, he registered merg (Ex.P-17).
Thus, it is clear that when the deceased was not traced and was missing on 27.05.2020 since 5:00 am.
The appellants searched her.
After that, missing person report was registered.

18. Witness-Babulal Yadav (PW-1) had stated that after six days of registering the missing person report, there was no clue regarding the deceased and after six days, her dead body was found in Jungle in hanging position.
The funda was made by saree.
19. Dr. Om Kesharwani (PW-2) conducted the autopsy over the dead body of the deceased on 02.06.2020 in Community Health Center, Devsar.
As per the statement of this witness, the dead body of the deceased was in shallow and decomposed position.
Her left hand and leg were completely decomposed.
Maggots were present in whole body, ligature around the neck was found measuring 1.5 meter x 25 centimeter and knot was 25 centimeter.
Both the hands were hanging downwards.
She was bearing blouse NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 10 CRA-898-2025 and underwear.
No external injuries were found.
The deceased died due to asphyxia.
As a result of hanging, the time of death was seven to eight days from the time of postmortem.
In the cross-examination, this witness had further clarified that there was no mark of the injury on the body of the deceased.
Thus, no ante-mortem injuries were found on the body of the deceased.

20. As per the statement of Neeraj Namdeo (PW-10), no FIR was lodged by the family members of the deceased and after merg inquiry, the FIR was registered on 04.06.2020 by the Police Officer Chhotelal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48355479/
5 itself whereas the merg was registered on 02.06.2020.

entities.text: Police Officer Chhotelal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Investigation Officer Neeraj Namdeo had stated that he lodged the FIR on the basis that the appellants were demanding motorcycle, gold chain and gold ring in dowry and harassing for that but as discussed above, this fact is not established and there are omnibus statements regarding the illicit relation of the appellant no.1 with appellant no.3.
No cogent evidence has been produced except the general statement.
21. The prosecution had not examined any witness of the village of the appellants where the deceased was residing.
No social Panchayat was organized by the family members of the deceased.

If there was demand of dowry and the appellants were harassing to fulfill the demand of dowry, the complainants would have surely complained to the relatives of the deceased and the villagers but no such fact has been brought on the record.

22. For the presumption under Section 114B of Evidence Act, there should be a direct nexus with the death and harassment for the dowry soon NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17451 11 CRA-898-2025 before woman's death and thus, there should be reasonable and close proximity between the demand and death.
In this case, the prosecution utterly failed to establish that any demand was made and the deceased was harassed for demand of dowry.
The other fact is that the appellant no.1-Chhotelal was not having physical relation with the deceased and having illicit relation with the appellant no.3.
This is also a type of cruelty and if this act was done wilfully with the intention to harass the deceased, reliable evidence is available on this point.
Hence, the conviction as held by the trial Court cannot be sustained.
Hence, the conviction of the appellants for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 304B of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act is quashed.
The appellants are acquitted from all the charges as stated above.
23. As a result, the sentence of the appellants passed by the trial Court is hereby quashed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
24. The appellants be released forthwith if not required in any other case.
The fine amount, if deposited, be refund to the appellants.
25. The case property be disposed of as per the order of the trial Court.
26. With the copy of the judgment, the record of the trial Court be sent back.
(VIVEK AGARWAL)
